title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
title_zh: 无需下游任务评估的编程智能体递归自我改进
abstract_en: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE), which integrates implementation mechanisms rather than selecting a single exploratory child to continue the lineage. At each generation, ELITE proposes diverse focused improvements, implements them independently from the same parent, and inspects the resulting programs to identify complementary, redundant, and conflicting mechanisms before reimplementing a compatible subset as one coherent descendant. No downstream task outcomes or task-solving trajectories of evolved candidates are used to guide evolution; only deterministic checks of structural and operational validity are used inside the loop. On SWE-bench Pro, ELITE improves the initial agent from 60.0% to 85.6%, compared with 86.7% for the Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) and 88.3% for the Huxley-Godel Machine (HGM), while using zero candidate task evaluations and reducing observed wall-clock evolution time by 8.8x and 3.2x, respectively, under the evaluated configurations. In cross-benchmark transfer without further adaptation, ELITE averages 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified and 69.3% on Polyglot. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of coding-agent self-improvement without downstream candidate task evaluation in our setting.
abstract_zh: 现有自我改进型编程智能体通常采用“评估后选择”（evaluate-and-select）：反复在下游任务上运行候选智能体，再据此决定哪些候选版本或演化分支得以延续。这使评估成本随探索范围扩大而上升，也可能促使智能体过度适配固定的基准分布。本文提出 Explore-then-Integrate（ELITE），用整合改进机制取代选拔单个候选版本。每一代从同一父版本出发，独立实现多项针对不同问题的改进，检查这些实现之间的互补、冗余和冲突，再将相容的机制重新实现为一个统一的后继版本。演化循环不使用候选智能体的下游任务结果或求解轨迹，仅通过确定性检查验证程序结构和运行的有效性。在 SWE-bench Pro 上，ELITE 将初始智能体的得分从 60.0% 提升至 85.6%，而 Darwin Godel Machine（DGM）和 Huxley-Godel Machine（HGM）分别达到 86.7% 和 88.3%。在论文评估配置下，ELITE 的演化用时分别约为 DGM 的 1/8.8 和 HGM 的 1/3.2。无需进一步适配，ELITE 在 SWE-bench Verified 和 Polyglot 上的平均得分分别为 73.3% 和 69.3%。
key_points_zh: ELITE 从同一父版本并行探索多项改进，根据实现机制的互补、冗余和冲突整合相容改进，而不是选出一个胜出的候选版本。
零候选任务评估仅指演化循环：循环内仍进行确定性的结构和运行检查，最终性能则通过下游基准衡量。
SWE-bench Pro 得分从 60.0% 升至 85.6%，略低于 DGM 的 86.7% 和 HGM 的 88.3%，但实测演化用时分别约为两者的 1/8.8 和 1/3.2。
无需进一步适配，在 SWE-bench Verified 和 Polyglot 上的平均得分分别为 73.3% 和 69.3%。

agent-harness-evolution.reason: 核心贡献是让编码代理迭代修改自身的可执行实现：从同一父代独立探索改进，合并兼容机制，并在循环内仅做确定性的结构和运行有效性检查。摘要报告了量化基线比较和跨基准迁移结果，但未提供消融，也未证明提出、整合或验证后续改进的机制本身得到改进。
